drapeaux.note: The original is French (Cour de cassation, 1st civil chamber, May 28, 1991) and no official English translation is known; faithful translation of the French quote, which could not be checked against a published English text. The url still points to the French official text on Legifrance.

titre: Huston v. Colorization: A Moral Right That a Contract Cannot Set Aside
accroche: In 1991, the Cour de cassation sets aside American law and contracts: Huston's heirs may invoke French moral rights.
contenu_vulgarise:
A French television channel wants to broadcast in color a film shot in black and white. The director is dead, and his heirs go to court. The case reaches the Cour de cassation (France's supreme court for civil matters), and the question it settles is not the one about color.

## One film, two ideas of the author

*The Asphalt Jungle*, known in France as *Quand la ville dort* (“When the City Sleeps”), is a black-and-white film by John Huston. The Turner company, which holds the producer's rights, has a colorized version made. The French channel La Cinq wants to broadcast it. Huston's heirs, joined by several legal entities including an artists' union, ask the French courts to forbid the broadcast in the name of respect for the integrity of the work.

The disagreement is less about color than about who the author is. Under American law of the time, as summed up by the legal scholars who comment on the case, a film fell among commissioned works (works made for hire): the producer was generally the author. Here, the contracts between the producer and the directors denied the directors the status of authors. In 1991, French law starts from the opposite idea: the author is the one who creates, and, according to Ginsburg and Sirinelli's analysis, his moral right is inalienable and perpetual.

## The ruling of May 28, 1991

The Paris court of appeal, on July 6, 1989, rejects the heirs' claim. It holds that the facts and the law it has found bar it from setting aside American law and putting the contracts to one side.

The first civil chamber of the Cour de cassation quashes the ruling in all its provisions. It relies on Article 1, paragraph 2, of the French law of July 8, 1964: no infringement may be made on the integrity of a literary or artistic work, whatever the State on whose territory the work was first disclosed. It adds, with Article 6 of the French law of March 11, 1957, that the author is vested with moral rights by the sole fact of creation. It describes these rules as laws of mandatory application (“lois d'application impérative”): they apply whatever the contract or foreign law says to the contrary. By applying American law and the contracts, the court of appeal refused to apply texts that it was bound to apply.

## What the ruling decides, and what it leaves open

The Court does not decide that colorization is an infringement of the work. Nor does it rule on the other grounds of the appeal. It decides only which law will answer the question, and sends the case back to the Versailles court of appeal. The texts cited are those the Court applies in 1991: the ruling says nothing of what today's rules provide, nor of what would happen in another French-speaking country.

What changes is the starting point. For the Court, it is not the contract that designates who holds moral rights; it is the fact of having created, even when the contract says the opposite.

carte.punch: An American black-and-white film, colorized: France applies its moral rights, not the contract.
carte.idee: In 1991, the Cour de cassation holds the French rules on the integrity of a work to be of mandatory application. John Huston's heirs may invoke them against the colorization of his film, despite American law and contracts that name no author. Whether there was an infringement remains to be judged.

quiz.question: Why does the Cour de cassation quash the Paris court of appeal's ruling in 1991?
choix: It holds that colorizing a film is always forbidden under French law
It holds that the French rules on the integrity of a work override contracts
It holds that the film had been shot in France and so fell under French law
It holds that Turner had not acquired the American producer's exploitation rights
quiz.explication: The Court holds that respect for the integrity of the work and moral rights are of mandatory application: the court of appeal refused to apply them, preferring American law and the contracts. It does not decide that every colorization is forbidden: it sends the case back to Versailles without itself ruling on the infringement. The protection applies whatever the State where the work was first disclosed, so the place of shooting is not the argument. The dispute does not concern Turner's acquisition of the rights.

quiz_supplementaire.question: According to the entry, what is the main disagreement between Turner and La Cinq on one side, and Huston's heirs on the other?
choix: The amount of fees owed to Turner for the colorized version
The term of copyright protection in the United States
Who should be considered the author of the film
The place where the film had been shot
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The entry places the disagreement on authorship, American law granting it to the producer and French law to the one who creates.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What did American law of the time say about the author of a commissioned film (work made for hire)?
choix: The director is always the author, whatever the contract
No person or entity can be named as author
Only the screenwriter can claim authorship
The producer is generally considered the author
quiz_supplementaire.explication: According to the American law summarized in the entry, a commissioned film makes the producer the author, and the contracts denied that status to the directors.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What does the Cour de cassation decide, and not decide, on May 28, 1991?
choix: It decides that colorization infringes the work and forbids the broadcast
It decides which law applies, but does not rule on whether colorization infringes the work
It decides that Turner must compensate Huston's heirs
It decides that French moral rights apply only to works first disclosed in France
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The Court quashes the ruling and sends the case back to Versailles without itself judging whether colorization infringes the work; it settles only the applicable law.
